text:
ana: Heads-up — I pushed the microwindow slotting experiment to staging-a this morning (changed default microwindow interval and slot allocator). Not great: KV hit rate dropped ~6 percentage points on the long-tail keys and small-req p95 jumped ~18–22ms. Sharing traces and quick numbers below.

mattg: Can you paste the perf summary and the exact config you applied?

ana: Sure — this was the change we tested: 
```yaml
microwindow:
  interval_ms: 6
  coalesce_jitter: 0.20
  slot_allocator: round_robin_with_backoff
  token_budget_target: 256
```
We originally had interval_ms: 4, coalesce_jitter: 0.12, token_budget_target: 300.

ana: Quick perf diffs (staging canary run id=2026-03-15_09):
```
requests: 12,200
avg_latency: 42ms -> 50ms
p95: 110ms -> 132ms
p99: 240ms -> 290ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.66
tokens/sec: 1.8k -> 1.6k
kv_evictions: baseline 1.2k -> 1.5k (+24%)
```

jamie: Which workload? Mostly short-context chats?

ana: Mostly short requests (<= 128 tokens). Kernel selector logs also show a shift — more int8_matmul_v2 choices for small sequences after the quant profile update last week. I don't think the kernel change directly caused kv misses but the traces show a timing shift that aligns with longer microwindow holding slots, which triggered more frequent KV evictions under the same memory pressure.

ravi: Hmm. So slot hold time increased and we now run out of KV slot space more often? Is eviction due to active slots or GC thresholds?

ana: Trace excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] slot_acquire(id=847): assigned window_end=+6ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] request_exec(kernel=int8_matmul_v2) start +2ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] kv_lookup(key=abc123) latency 4.2ms -> 9.0ms (queueing/backpressure)
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] kv_eviction(reason=slot_pressure) -> evicted_keys=3
```

mattg: Could be two interacting effects: increased microwindow interval -> higher concurrency within a window -> more KV working set live -> evictions. And kernel shifts can slightly change timing so eviction boundaries align worse.

ravi: Quick mitigation: reduce interval_ms to 5 and lower jitter to 0.12, or raise token_budget_target so each batch consumes more tokens and we have fewer distinct slots active. Try ablation: interval=5, jitter=0.12, token_budget=320.

ana: I ran that ablation on a small canary (run id=2026-03-15_11). Results after 6k requests: 
```
requests: 6,100
avg_latency: 44ms
p95: 118ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.69
kv_evictions: 1.33k (-11% vs broken experiment)
tokens/sec: 1.73k
```
Seems better — p95 improved ~14ms vs the 6ms interval run and kv_hit partially recovered.

jamie: Nice. Any change in kernel selection behavior in that ablation run?

ana: Kernel choices stayed mixed, still a bias toward int8_matmul_v2 for short sequences. Flame sample shows CPU/GPU time distribution slightly different but not alarming. The main win seems to be fewer concurrent live slots reducing KV pressure.

mattg: OK. Actionable plan?

ravi: Short-term: rollback the 6ms -> 4ms baseline change and apply intermediate patch (interval=5ms, jitter=0.12, token_budget=320) to staging, monitor kv_hit and p95 for 24h. Medium-term: update slot allocator so it is eviction-aware (prefer keys with recent KV hits) and add per-slot mem accounting so we can throttle slot admission before eviction thrash. Also add a trace tag for kernel selection vs kv_lookup latency correlation.

ana: I'll open a PR for the intermediate patch and add dashboards for kv_evictions and slot_hold_time. Also putting an E2E perf test in the canary harness to surface this interaction earlier.

deploy-bot: canary roll scheduled: staging-a -> intermediate-patch (interval=5ms). Estimated completion 1955554390. :rocket:

mattg: Thanks — annotating the perf regression ticket with these traces and the ablation results. We should also check if quant profile change last week changed kernel latency distribution.

ana: Good call. I'll run a targeted kernel-latency sweep against the quant profile and attach results to the ticket.

ravi: If the allocator change is a bigger lift, we can also try increasing KV capacity on a subset of hosts as a temporary safety valve.

ana: noted. I'll start with the intermediate patch + monitoring and post updates here. :white_check_mark:
